questions.question: In PM CoCrFeMnNi, does the negative stacking fault energy at cryogenic temperatures (<260 K) persist if structural relaxation in the faulted supercell is included, given the current model assumes a fixed c/a ratio and no relaxation?
questions.rationale: The paper attributes negative SFE to hcp stability but omits structural relaxation and assumes an ideal c/a ratio; including these could reverse the predicted negative SFE, fundamentally altering the expected deformation mechanism (nano-twinning vs. slip).
questions.decision_use: Determine whether the predicted negative SFE and associated twin-dominated deformation at cryogenic temperatures is an artifact of the rigid supercell approximation or a robust physical feature of the alloy.
answer_requirements: Compute stacking fault energy (γ_isf) for the hcp-fcc fault interface in PM CoCrFeMnNi at 50 K allowing full ionic relaxation of the supercell atoms and using a non-ideal c/a ratio derived from the relaxed structure.
evidence_spans: the γ isf of PM CoCrFeMnNi is predicted from the LSF calculations to increase from −17 mJ m −2 at 50 K, reach zero at ~260 K and keep rising to 31 mJ m −2 at 1000 K
The structural relaxation in the faulted supercell was omitted.
an ideal c / a ratio of 8/3 was employed for the hcp structure

questions.question: Does the magneto-volume coupling mechanism alone explain the SFE increase in PM CoCrFeMnNi between 260 K and 1000 K, or do non-magnetic thermal contributions (phonons) play a significant role in the SFE trend observed in this regime?
questions.rationale: The paper attributes the positive SFE dependence to magneto-volume coupling, but phonon contributions to the free energy difference between fcc and hcp phases are unknown; determining the phonon contribution is necessary to isolate the magnetic mechanism for alloy design.
questions.decision_use: Decide whether to focus computational resources on refining magnetic models (LSF/DLM) or to incorporate full phonon calculations (e.g., quasiharmonic approximation) to accurately predict SFE at elevated temperatures.
answer_requirements: Compare the calculated SFE trend with and without explicit phonon contributions to the Gibbs free energy difference between fcc and hcp phases in PM CoCrFeMnNi over the 260 K–1000 K range.
evidence_spans: The positive temperature dependence of γ isf is ultimately dominated by the magneto-volume coupling at thermal excitations.

However, at finite temperature, a proper account of magnetic excitations, both transversal and longitudinal spin fluctuations (LSFs), is of particular challenge for magnetic transition metals and alloys like the Cantor alloy, owing to the lack of a complete theory for itinerant electron magnetism [24] , [25] .
